title: [Elopement of Althea Stone] "…Mrs. Stone's mansion, No. 2035 Prairie avenue … the Stone's 'steamboat' house, so called from the numerous pretty galleries of fancy woodwork which adorn its exterior."
creator: National Police Gazette (New York)
found_via: IA full-text search '"2035 prairie"'; passage read on the page image (IIIF crop)
notes: Read on the page: "he never made more than two or three calls at Mrs. Stone's mansion, No. 2035 Prairie avenue. The Cunninghams live on the north side, miles from the Stone's 'steamboat' house, so called from the numerous pretty galleries of fancy woodwork which adorn its exterior." Bearing: 2035 (Mrs. Horatio O. Stone's house, occupied by her through 1904 and to c. 1912) was a 'MANSION' known for tiers of ornamental WOODEN GALLERIES/VERANDAS on its exterior — consistent with the 1898 Tribune vignette (detached house with a broad columned veranda, cgs-tribune-1898-01-09-death-strip) and with the 1934 ad (corner building, 30 rooms, 9 baths). TENSION with the library and collection: the library models 2031–2035 as a trio of 25-ft limestone-fronted townhouses of 1869 (Reid nomination p. 13), and the Robinson 1886 plate shows a continuous row of three brick houses with stone fronts there (cgs-2031-robinson-1886). 2035 is the row's END house on the 21st Street corner (the Evening Post's 1869 'marble-front house on northeast corner of Prairie-av. and Twenty-first-st.'), so the 'galleries of fancy woodwork' were most likely verandas added on its exposed front and 21st Street flank — the 1898 vignette's broad columned veranda. Model 2035 in 1904 as the corner end of the stone-fronted row WITH wooden galleries/veranda, not as a plain row front; its 1934 '30 rooms' suggests it was larger than its two neighbours (deeper or extended).
